# Introduction

Since moving to Los Angeles for graduate school, a common thing I have heard is that "LA used to be better" because "tons" of businesses closed as a result of the pandemic. While I believe this can be said for almost every city in the world, I wanted to explore just how impactful the pandemic really was for Los Angeles-based businesses, using the "Listing of All Businesses" dataset from the Los Angeles Office of Finance. This dataset contains all active and inactive registered business locations, with "active" being defined as a business whose owner has not notified the Office of Finance of a cease of operations. The dataset contains relevant variables such as location, location start and end date, council district, and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) description. The primary question I will try to answer with this dataset is: How did the  number of business-location closures in Los Angeles change during the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2020 - May 5,2023) compared with the pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods? A follow-up quiestion that I will explore later is: Which industries experienced the greatest changes in closure frequency during the pandemic?

The time range for the pandemic was defined as March 11, 2020 to May 5, 2023 based on these references:

1.  https://www.cdc.gov/museum/timeline/covid19.html
2.  https://www.who.int/news/item/05-05-2023-statement-on-the-fifteenth-meeting-of-the-international-health-regulations-(2005)-emergency-committee-regarding-the-coronavirus-disease-(covid-19)-pandemic

# Data Preparation

The "Listing of All Businesses" dataset was obtained from the City of Los Angeles Open Data Portal and is maintained by the Los Angeles Office of Finance (https://data.lacity.org/Administration-Finance/Listing-of-All-Businesses/r4uk-afju/about_data). Because the primary question is focused on business-location closures, observations without a location end date were classified as active and excluded. Variables that are not needed to answer the primary question, such as "mailing address" and "location description" were also removed. Dates were converted into R date objects as well. Invalid dates, those whose end dates occur before their start date, were removed. According to the data library, observations whose council district has "0" are out of the city, so these observations were removed.

Date-based categories were then created, with "Pre-Pandemic" referring to any location end date prior to March 11, 2020. "Pandemic" refers to any location end date between March 11, 2020 and May 5, 2023. "Post-Pandemic" refers to any location end date after May 5, 2023. Future location end dates, those that have not happened yet, were removed from the "Closures" data frame. The cutoff date for this was set as October 15, 2026, the date this dataset was downloaded. Acknowledging that the "Pre-Pandemic" category extends all the way back to 1977, a second data frame was created, "Closures_Adjusted," to answer potential follow-up questions. Here, periods were restricted to 1,151 days, which was the length of the Pandemic. "Pre-Pandemic was defined as any location end date between January 15, 2017 and March 10, 2020. "Post-Pandemic was defined as any location end date between May 6, 2023 and June 29, 2026. "Pandemic" was unchanged. For other potential follow up questions and visualizations, "Closure Month," "Closure Year," and "Closure.Month.Date" variables were created.

```{r}
# Read in data. Create Original Data Frame. Re-format dates. 
All_Businesses <- read.csv("C:/Users/nweit/Downloads/Listing_of_All_Businesses_20261015.csv")

All_Businesses$LOCATION.START.DATE <- as.Date(All_Businesses$LOCATION.START.DATE, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
All_Businesses$LOCATION.END.DATE <- as.Date(All_Businesses$LOCATION.END.DATE, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

# Create Closures Data Frame. Remove Unnecessary Variables. Invalid Dates Removed. Removed Out-of-City Businesses. Establish Cutoff End Date. Create "Period", "Closure.Month", and "Closure.Year" Variables. 
Closures <- All_Businesses[!is.na(All_Businesses$LOCATION.END.DATE),]
Closures <- Closures[,!names(Closures) %in% c("MAILING.ZIP.CODE","DBA.NAME","LOCATION.DESCRIPTION","MAILING.CITY","MAILING.ADDRESS")]

Closures <- Closures[is.na(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE) | Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE >= Closures$LOCATION.START.DATE,]

Closures <- Closures[!is.na(Closures$COUNCIL.DISTRICT) & Closures$COUNCIL.DISTRICT >= 1 & Closures$COUNCIL.DISTRICT <=15,]

Fixed_Date <- as.Date("2026-10-15")
Closures <- Closures[Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE <= Fixed_Date,]

Closures$Period <- ifelse(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE < as.Date("2020-03-11"),"Pre-Pandemic", ifelse(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE <= as.Date("2023-05-05"),"Pandemic","Post-Pandemic"))

Closures$Period <- factor(Closures$Period, levels = c("Pre-Pandemic","Pandemic","Post-Pandemic"))

Closures$Closure.Month <- format(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE, format = "%m")
Closures$Closure.Year <- format(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE, format = "%Y")
Closures$Closure.Month.Date <- as.Date(format(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE, "%Y-%m-01"))


# Create Closures_Adjusted with January 15, 2017 and June 29,2026 as the Cutoff End Dates.
Closures_Adjusted <- Closures[Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE >= as.Date("2017-01-15") & Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE <= as.Date("2026-06-29"),]
```

# Exploratory Analysis

For the Exploratory Analysis, I will be using both the "Closures" and "Closures_Adjusted" data frames. "Closures" includes all records dating back to 1977 and "Closures_Adjusted" includes all records dating back to December 10, 2016. For each visualization, "Historic Data" will refer to the "Closures" data frame and "Adjusted Data" will refer to the "Closures_Adjusted" data frame.

```{r}
library(knitr)

# Summary Table that includes Size, Range, and Other Dataset Characteristics (Historic Data)
Missing_Industry <- is.na(Closures$PRIMARY.NAICS.DESCRIPTION) | trimws(Closures$PRIMARY.NAICS.DESCRIPTION) == ""
Missing_Location <- is.na(Closures$LOCATION) | trimws(Closures$LOCATION) == ""
Missing_NAICS <- is.na(Closures$NAICS) | trimws(Closures$NAICS) == ""

Table <- data.frame(Characteristic = c("Business-Location Closures", "Earliest Closure Date", "Latest Closure Date", "Unique Location Accounts", "Missing NAICS Codes", "Missing Industry Descriptions", "Missing Locations"), Value = c(format(nrow(Closures), big.mark = ","), format(min(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE, na.rm = TRUE)), format(max(Closures$LOCATION.END.DATE, na.rm = TRUE)), format(length(unique(Closures$LOCATION.ACCOUNT..)), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_NAICS), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_Industry), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_Location), big.mark = ",")))

knitr::kable(Table, col.names = c("Dataset Characteristic", "Value"), caption = "Business-Closure Characterisitcs (Historic Data)")

# Summary Table that includes Size, Range, and Other Dataset Characteristics (Adjusted Data)
Missing_Industry <- is.na(Closures_Adjusted$PRIMARY.NAICS.DESCRIPTION) | trimws(Closures_Adjusted$PRIMARY.NAICS.DESCRIPTION) == ""
Missing_Location <- is.na(Closures_Adjusted$LOCATION) | trimws(Closures_Adjusted$LOCATION) == ""
Missing_NAICS <- is.na(Closures_Adjusted$NAICS) | trimws(Closures_Adjusted$NAICS) == ""

Table <- data.frame(Characteristic = c("Business-Location Closures", "Earliest Closure Date", "Latest Closure Date", "Unique Location Accounts", "Missing NAICS Codes", "Missing Industry Descriptions", "Missing Locations"), Value = c(format(nrow(Closures_Adjusted), big.mark = ","), format(min(Closures_Adjusted$LOCATION.END.DATE, na.rm = TRUE)), format(max(Closures_Adjusted$LOCATION.END.DATE, na.rm = TRUE)), format(length(unique(Closures_Adjusted$LOCATION.ACCOUNT..)), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_NAICS), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_Industry), big.mark = ","), format(sum(Missing_Location), big.mark = ",")))

knitr::kable(Table, col.names = c("Dataset Characteristic", "Value"), caption = "Business-Closure Characterisitcs (Adjusted Data)")

```

```{r}
# Closures by Period (Historic Data)
Period_Count <- as.data.frame(table(Closures$Period))
names(Period_Count) <- c("Period","Closures")
Period_Count$Percentage <- round(100*Period_Count$Closures / sum(Period_Count$Closures),1)
knitr::kable(Period_Count, col.names = c("Period", "Closures", "Percentage"), caption = "Business-Location Closures by Period (Historic Data)")

# Closures by Period (Adjusted Data)
Period_Count <- as.data.frame(table(Closures_Adjusted$Period))
names(Period_Count) <- c("Period","Closures")
Period_Count$Percentage <- round(100*Period_Count$Closures / sum(Period_Count$Closures),1)
knitr::kable(Period_Count, col.names = c("Period", "Closures", "Percentage"), caption = "Business-Location Closures by Period (Adjusted Data)")
```

```{r}
# Closures by Year (Historic Data)
Yearly_Closures <- as.data.frame(table(Closures$Closure.Year))
names(Yearly_Closures) <- c("Year", "Closures")
Yearly_Closures$Year <- as.integer(as.character(Yearly_Closures$Year))

# Closures by Year (Adjusted Data)
Yearly_Closures <- as.data.frame(table(Closures_Adjusted$Closure.Year))
names(Yearly_Closures) <- c("Year", "Closures")
Yearly_Closures$Year <- as.integer(as.character(Yearly_Closures$Year))

Year_Count <- table(Closures_Adjusted$Closure.Year)
All_Years <- seq(min(Closures_Adjusted$Closure.Year, na.rm = TRUE), max(Closures_Adjusted$Closure.Year, na.rm = TRUE))
Yearly_Closures <- data.frame(Year = All_Years, Closures = as.numeric(Year_Count[as.character(All_Years)]))

barplot(Yearly_Closures$Closures, names.arg = Yearly_Closures$Year, las = 2, col = "blue", xlab = "Closure Year", ylab = "Number of Closures", main = "Business-Location Closures by Year (Adjusted Data)", sub = "Note: 2016 and 2026 are Incomplete Years. 2016 begins on December 17, 2016 and 2026 ends on October 15, 2026.")
```

```{r}
Complete_Periods <- Closures_Adjusted
Period_Totals <- as.data.frame(table(Complete_Periods$Period))
names(Period_Totals) <- c("Period", "Total_Closures")
Period_Totals$Mean_Daily_Closures <- Period_Totals$Total_Closures / 1151
knitr::kable(Period_Totals, col.names = c("Period", "Total Closures", "Mean Daily Closures"), caption = "Business-Location Closures by Period")

Monthly_Closures <- aggregate(rep(1,nrow(Complete_Periods)), by=list(Closures_Periods = Complete_Periods$Closure.Month.Date, Period = Complete_Periods$Period), FUN = sum)
names(Monthly_Closures)[3] <- "Closures"

Monthly_Mean <- aggregate(Closures ~ Period, data = Monthly_Closures, FUN = mean)

Monthly_Median <- aggregate(Closures ~ Period, data = Monthly_Closures, FUN = median)

Monthly_SD <- aggregate(Closures ~ Period, data = Monthly_Closures, FUN = sd)

Monthly_Min <- aggregate(Closures ~ Period, data = Monthly_Closures, FUN = min)

Monthly_Max <- aggregate(Closures ~ Period,data = Monthly_Closures,FUN = max)

Period_Summary <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "Period"),list(Monthly_Mean, Monthly_Median, Monthly_SD, Monthly_Min, Monthly_Max))

names(Period_Summary) <- c("Period", "Mean", "Median", "SD", "Minimum", "Maximum")

Period_Summary$Months <- as.numeric(table(Monthly_Closures$Period)[Period_Summary$Period])

Period_Summary <- Period_Summary[,c("Period", "Mean", "Median", "SD", "Minimum", "Maximum")]

knitr::kable(Period_Summary, digits = 1, col.names = c("Period", "Mean", "Median", "Standard Deviation", "Minimum", "Maximum"),caption = "Monthly Business-Location Closures by Period")

boxplot(Closures ~ Period, data = Monthly_Closures, col = c("blue", "red", "green"), border = "gray", xlab = "Period", ylab = "Monthly Closures", main = "Distribuition of Monthly Closures by Period")
```

# Preliminary Results

Primary Question: How did the number of business-location closures in Los Angeles change during the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2020 - May 5,2023) compared with the pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods?

The historic data reveals that, after data-cleaning, 648,537 businesses closed from November 14, 1977 and October 14, 2026, with 78.8% (511,350) of those closures occurring before the Pandemic. 10.3% (66,986) occurred during the Pandemic and 10.8% (70,201) occurred after the Pandemic. The year with the largest number of closures appears to be 2013. The month with the largest number of closures
